name: Financial filings
description: Companies, annual and quarterly filings, statements, line items, reported values, segments, auditors and risk factors.
purpose: Turn annual and quarterly reports into a graph of reported financial facts, each tied to its company, line item, period, segment and unit, alongside auditors, executives and disclosed risks.
scope: In scope: filing metadata, reporting periods, the primary financial statements, line items and reported values, segment breakdowns, audit opinions, executives and risk factors. Out of scope: market prices, analyst estimates, ratio calculation and full XBRL taxonomy modelling.
stories: As an equity analyst I want revenue and net income per company, period and segment with units so that I can compare performance across filings without retyping tables.
As a compliance reviewer I want each filing linked to its auditor, opinion type and certifying executives so that I can spot qualified opinions and changes of auditor.
As a risk analyst I want disclosed risk factors grouped by category per filing so that I can track how a company's risk disclosures change over time.
cqs: Which filings has a company submitted, with form type and filing date?
What reporting period does each filing cover, with start and end dates?
What value, in which currency or unit, did a company report for a given line item in a given period?
How is a line item broken down by operating or geographic segment for a period?
Which line items roll up into a given total line item?
Which financial statements does a filing contain, and which values does each report?
Which audit firm audited a filing and what type of opinion did it issue?
Which risk factors, by category, are disclosed in a given filing?
Who are the executives of a company and which of them certified each filing?
